body:
Hmmm, I'm fine with the PR as-is. But I am not opposed to doing something like the following. 

1. Detect if a user shader reads/writes `BINORMAL` (current if `BINORMAL` is used we detect it and add `#define TANGENT_USED` to the shader, this should be changed to `BINORMAL_USED`)
2. Continue calculating `BINORMAL` and interpolating  if `BINORMAL_USED`
3. If not `BINORMAL_USAGE` derive `BINORMAL` in the fragment shader. 

This adds a bit of complexity. But will maintain compatibility and it will be a straight upgrade in most cases (for both performance and correctness). I am not worried about the slightly different behaviour in each case. Since the former case would only be for users who read/write `BINORMAL` in a custom shader which is relatively rare and likely has totally different behaviour from what is currently in the build in shader (and ultimately won't be affected by this change)

Point one is as simple as changing:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/34cdc6e43f4a821d3a863366f10474a844dd077c/drivers/gles3/storage/material_storage.cpp#L1367

to `actions.usage_defines["BINORMAL"] = "# define BINORMAL USED";` and adding:

```
#if defined(BINORMAL_USED) && !defined(TANGENT_USED)
#define TANGENT_USED
#endif
```

One other reason I didn't want to pursue this immediately is this would require changes in the decoding scaffolding which would conflict with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/120901. Maybe the fragment reconstruction rework could be a separate PR?
